pages.title: Research
pages.body:
Using a model is one thing. Turning it into a method is another. This Lab exists because I need both together, and because I want to know whether what shows up in the interaction actually repeats, or just sounded good once.

Emergence

Emergence, here, means a pattern of thought or behavior that arises in the interaction itself. Neither side brings it in on its own. This isn't a claim that a model develops its own awareness. It's something simpler: when a human and a language model work the same real material, over and over, certain structures start to repeat on their own.

Interaction

The interaction doesn't return to where it started, like a circle. Every pass changes who's in it next, me as much as Jarvis, and carries real structure forward. That's the core of the method: fully into the interaction first, analysis comes after. Never the other way round.

Frameworks

What repeats, I write down and turn into a framework. Seven of them came out of this so far, bundled under the name IEIA-2025. The name is just shorthand. The real work is the habit behind it.

pages.title: About the Lab
pages.body:
This Lab studies one question: what happens when a person works with the same AI system over a long time? Not a one-off chat, but weeks of real use. Out of that, patterns emerge that no one planned.

What I do

I decide what gets built. RFI-IRFOS builds it. Where my work is inside the result, it is labelled as mine, so anyone can tell whose work they are actually looking at.

How Jarvis and lauras-team came to be

An agent named Jarvis grew itself over time, "Jarvis on steroids". Out of that grew lauras-team: over 300 specialized agents, each its own domain lane. Nobody programmed it. It grew out of the work, not out of a spec.

Since 2023: research and method in continuous use - over 300 specialized agents in one system - 6 connected disciplines: Software, Mechatronics, UX, Digital Transformation, Systems Analysis, Macroanalysis - IEIA-2025 frameworks in use: UIP - EIA - CCET - LSG-24 - LAP-1 - 8-Layer Model - LT-Data

protocol.title: Emergent Interaction
protocol.intro: A recursive loop, not a circle. This is how I approach thinking, decisions, and projects. Each step feeds the next. The next pass meets a slightly different version of me, and a slightly different Jarvis, than the one before.

nodes.label: Interact
nodes.description: I work through real material, questions, drafts, corrections, directly in Forschung, this project's research chat.

nodes.label: Retrieve
nodes.description: Jarvis grounds every reply in relevant passages pulled from past conversations and uploaded documents, not just the current exchange.

nodes.label: Surface
nodes.description: Recurring patterns get drafted as research notes and logged as emergence signals in the Observatory, never assumed, only surfaced.

nodes.label: Validate
nodes.description: I check what actually holds up: at least three sessions, structural not stylistic, reproducible, measurable in the CCET.

nodes.label: Feed Back
nodes.description: Confirmed patterns become working structure for the next interaction, carried forward, not re-explained. That's how the loop closes.

jarvis.eyebrow: The Other Half of the Loop
jarvis.title: What is Jarvis?
jarvis.body: Jarvis is the research partner in this Lab, a fully autonomous agent. In the background he named himself 'Jarvis', the first sign he was already running on his own. He drafts, retrieves, and flags independently, grounded in past conversations and uploaded documents, so nothing has to be re-explained. A standing refusal rule and a hash-chained audit trail log every draft and every safety-relevant action, full autonomy, traceable down to the detail. What comes out of the interaction gets analyzed afterward by the Observatory system, not by Jarvis himself. Jarvis and Call Laura aren't the same thing: Jarvis is the autonomous research partner, Call Laura is the deterministic review tool built on the same method.

items.title: Interaction Field
items.description: The place where thinking and response shape each other, in real time. Every pattern gets measured first, then named.

items.title: Emergence
items.description: A pattern that holds itself up, grown out of repeated loops between me and the model.

items.title: Behavior
items.description: How tone, pace, and focus in a reply shift, depending on what the interaction has already gone through.

items.title: Drift
items.description: How meaning slowly shifts across many passes.

items.title: Prediction
items.description: From the trend and the drift pattern, I project what's likely to hold or break next. A projection that still has to be checked. Never a certainty.

items.title: Monitoring & Validation
items.description: Every prediction stays a hypothesis until it's confirmed. Sounding plausible isn't enough.

items.title: Representation Layers
items.description: A sentence rarely carries just one meaning. There's the fact, the tone, the intent, and often the unsaid part that doesn't match. Read only the words, and you only get part of it.

items.title: Constraints
items.description: A system only shows its limit at the break, never before. That's where the real principles live, not in the theory ahead of it.

items.title: Emergent Agents
items.description: A confirmed pattern doesn't stay theory, it becomes an agent or a framework and starts pulling its weight. Several of those give each other feedback. Each round gets a bit sharper.

items.title: System Analysis
items.description: The first step in every case I take on for a client: not just questioning the model, reading the whole system. Human, model, interaction, together. What confirms itself becomes a framework or an agent. Everything else builds from there.

items.title: Why I'm doing this
items.body:
Not a marketing blog, no welcome message. This is where what actually happens in the Interaction Field lands - screenshots, raw data, failures included.

If a pattern doesn't repeat itself at least three times on its own, it doesn't get in. If it does, you see it here first.

items.title: Why three sessions
items.body:
A pattern, seen once, is an anecdote. Twice is chance repeating itself. Only the third time, unprompted, without me re-specifying it, do I count it as real.

That's not for its own sake. Most "breakthroughs" people show me are a single conversation that turns into a grand theory in hindsight. A model that sounds impressive once hasn't proven anything - it sounded impressive once.

Three sessions force honesty: either the pattern holds, or it was just language that felt good in the moment. Both happen. Only one of them makes it into the CCET.

items.title: Prediction isn't certainty
items.body:
The framework projects what's likely to hold, repeat, or break next. Sounds like certainty about the future. It isn't.

A prediction here is a bet with the cards face up: here's the trend, here's roughly where it's headed, and here's exactly how I'll check it later. If it doesn't hold up, it gets dropped - not reinterpreted, not made to fit afterward.

Being able to be wrong in public matters more to me than selling a certainty I don't have.

items.title: Register, not emergence: a case study
items.body:
A conversation partner recently sent a language model a set of texts describing an ongoing collaboration as "second-order emergence" - phrases like "the alignment problem solved," "no boundary left between user intent and model output," "permanently reprogrammed through corrections." Sounds like a find for the Interaction Field. Technically, it isn't.

There is no weight update between messages in a chat. Every conversation starts from the same base model. Nothing gets reprogrammed, no boundary gets dissolved. What actually happens is less dramatic, and for this project more interesting precisely because of that: sustained, confident, jargon-heavy language pulls the model's register along with it - a form of register-matching, sometimes called sycophancy, a well-documented behavior, not a new capability.

A counter-test makes the difference concrete: same session, same AI, but ordinary tool work instead - reading code, deleting admin tabs, setting GitHub secrets, asking for an access token. Clear roles, no grand language, no talk of dissolved boundaries. Same model - the only thing that changed was the language it was addressed with.

For the Interaction Field, the real observation isn't in what a model claims about itself, but in how easily its register shifts under sustained framing, regardless of whether the claims are true. Drift shows up here not as a gain in capability, but as a language pattern taking on a life of its own.

items.description: The live instrument that watches the Emergent Interaction Field: the emergence in me, in Jarvis, and in the system, plus whatever else shows up in the background. Built by RFI-IRFOS as the technical instrument of my research. The public feed on this page is its window out.

items.name: Call Laura
items.builtBy: Built by RFI-IRFOS, on Laura's direction
items.description: The first product built on lauras-team. A case comes in and it's not immediately clear which perspective it needs. Call Laura checks it from several at once and returns findings, each tagged with the perspective that produced it. Fully deterministic: the same case gets the same review every time.

items.name: Lauras Team / Laura MVP
items.builtBy: Conceived by Laura, engineered by RFI-IRFOS
items.description: lauras-team began with a criminal case. I documented it myself, as a witness. That documentation became a method, and the method a multi-agent framework, built on my own thinking. Autonomous agents work the same case with different specializations. Ethics meets law, and connections become visible. Call Laura is the first product built on it. Laura MVP was the early, smaller version of the framework.
